summary: @servicetitan/anvil2 preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727KB sibling payload
details: The package declares itself as a React UI component library but ships a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, at `npm install` time, downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and uses it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line JavaScript blob obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style string-array rotation (`WV8StW`) and a hex/char-code lookup table, and cannot be statically audited without deobfuscation. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated using hex-suffixed identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`) and per-function string-lookup object literals (`YCZJE`, `QkQej`, `WuGMv`, `TdVzu`) that indirect every method call and string constant, including references to `--version`, `musl`, and `/etc/os-release`. A UI component library has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate language runtime and use it to execute an opaque bundled payload against the installer's host. The Bun-based execution path also evades Node-focused install-time scanners. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: install-time fetch of a runtime plus execution of an opaque, obfuscated sibling blob whose behavior on the installer's machine is not auditable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
